派對號角屬氣鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs編號412.131。操作時手: The party horn is an aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 412.131. Hold it by the mouthpiece end, put the mouthpiece in your mouth and blow: the paper tube unrolls and gives out a horn-like note; when you stop blowing, the coiled metal or plastic strip inside draws the tube back in. Modern variants use a plastic mouthpiece, which keeps saliva from ruining the paper tube.
派對號角為紙製氣鳴樂器，發聲分類為412.131，地區標記為歐洲。其於二十世紀初: The party horn is a paper aerophone, sounding classification 412.131, with Europe given as its region. It became a party giveaway in the early twentieth century and is common at birthday parties, at New Year and at other celebrations. Modern variants add a plastic mouthpiece, which reduces damage to the paper tube from moisture in the mouth; inside the paper tube there is usually a metal or plastic spring, so that it retracts quickly after blowing, and some have feathers at the end that vibrate in the airflow. The instrument has also entered public events and records: on 21 November 2009, 6091 people in Tokyo blew them at once; in September 2020 David Rush and Eirinn Hannon of Idaho blew 108 times in a minute, breaking the previous record of 78.
派對號角的音色尖銳刺耳，帶有明亮而喧鬧的特徵，屬於高頻率的噪音製造工具。其音域集: The party horn's timbre is sharp and piercing, bright and noisy: it belongs among the makers of high-frequency noise. Its range sits in the treble, and it sounds like a crude whistle or a rowdy variant of the trumpet. The colour is rough and mechanical, lacking the warmth and refinement of traditional instruments. The resonance depends mainly on the vibration of the paper and on the flutter of a reed or membrane inside, which gives an unstable, slightly metallic sound. Next to a proper brass instrument such as the trumpet or trombone, round and full, the party horn is more aggressive and more primitive; next to a whistle it is harsher and has only one layer. Its particular noisiness makes it the ideal tool for making a festive atmosphere: in essence its timbre belongs to the non-musical sounds people make on purpose.
